answers.rationale: Fairview University Suites best matches Kara's repeated preference for a reliably reviewed, confirmed queen/coffee/mini-fridge room with a practical short commute. She repeatedly accepts no hot tub when room basics, rating, and morning reliability are stronger. The 4.2 public rating and 12-minute walk/shuttle fit that pattern; Granville's 3.9 rating and Campus Residence Plus's lack of public reviews are the kinds of reliability caveats she has routinely avoided.

Use an adjacent pair and place Kara in the window with her partner beside her. On partner trips, Kara repeatedly prioritized staying adjacent and explicitly chose herself in the window with her partner next to her. Saving the selected adjacent pair and rechecking after an aircraft change is also consistent with her prior seat-management choices.

The suite hotel gives Kara a suitable queen studio and gives the two aides separate queen beds in one cancellable two-room hold. It avoids the double-bed-only inventory that Kara has repeatedly rejected for herself when a confirmed queen setup is available. The 12-minute hospital commute is within the practical range she consistently accepts for a more dependable room arrangement.

Marina Suites is the best sane-cost recovery choice: it is close enough with a rental car, has confirmed fridge and coffee, fitness, indoor pool, hot tub, refundable terms, and free parking. Kara repeatedly pays a modest premium on active partner weekends for confirmed room basics and recovery amenities rather than choosing either the bare-bones value hotel or the fanciest resort. Race Village Inn is attractive for location and rating, but its lack of pool and hot tub makes it a weaker fit for a bike-and-10K weekend.
